primary_claim: RoPE-based language models trained with learned per-token (and per-layer) position increments instead of a fixed +1 increment encode interpretable linguistic structure -- larger increments at word/sentence/document boundaries and smaller increments within words -- while having a barely detectable effect on training loss and perplexity.

effect.metric: reduction in learned position increment (space token) for real vs reversed multi-word entity order, per layer
effect.value: 51-78% smaller space increment for real order ('New York') vs reversed ('York New') at layers L1-L5, p as low as 3e-8

stated_future_work: find summary positions where inspecting with other tools would be useful (e.g. the last token before a large positional increment)
understand what a model is looking for at each layer, especially open-ended investigation of larger models
explore the structure with different datasets, e.g. code
determine the best way to train per-layer position increment vectors
finish grafting learned per-token position increments onto an existing pretrained model (SmolLM2-1.7B) and inspect per-layer results
limitations_stated: only trained a small number of models with very little variation between architectures
gradient signal for increments to be useful is weak since they didn't meaningfully improve loss; only a small number of models/layers inspected
never trained a large model from scratch; unclear if fine-tuned models learn the same increments as from-scratch training
didn't train per-layer position increment vectors on a large model
quote: I consistently found that the learned position increments have a barely detectable effect on loss and perplexity.
